title: LongAdder — striped cells, reduces contention vs AtomicLong, when to prefer

s1_definition.profdef: `LongAdder` (Java 8) is a high-throughput counter that reduces CAS contention by STRIPING — instead of all threads CAS-ing on ONE variable (AtomicLong), each thread increments its OWN cell in an array. `sum()` adds all cells. Under low contention: uses a single `base` variable (like AtomicLong). Under high contention: CAS on base fails → thread allocated a Cell → increments its own cell → zero contention! `@Contended` on each Cell prevents false sharing. 5-10x faster than AtomicLong under 16+ threads. Trade-off: `sum()` is NOT atomic — it reads base + all cells without synchronization, so concurrent increments may produce a slightly stale sum. Use LongAdder when: high write contention, exact real-time sum not required (counters, statistics, metrics).
s1_definition.analogy: **AtomicLong** = ONE shared counter at the entrance. 100 people trying to click it simultaneously → everyone fighting over the same button (CAS retry). **LongAdder** = 10 separate counters at 10 different doors. Each person clicks the nearest counter. End of day: manager walks around and ADDS UP all 10 counters. No fighting! 10x faster! But: while the manager is adding, someone might click another counter → sum slightly off (acceptable for daily totals, not for real-time balance).
s1_definition.oneliner: LongAdder: per-thread striped cells → zero contention → 5-10x faster than AtomicLong. sum() = base + Σcells (not atomic). Use for counters/metrics. AtomicLong for exact real-time value.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** `LongAdder` (Java 8) is a high-throughput counter that reduces CAS contention by STRIPING — instead of all threads CAS-ing on ONE variable (AtomicLong), each thread increments its OWN cell in an array. `sum()` adds all cells. Under low contention: uses a single `base` variable (like AtomicLong). Under high contention: CAS on base fails → thread allocated a Cell → increments its own cell → zero contention! `@Contended` on each Cell prevents false sharing. 5-10x faster than AtomicLong under 16+ threads. Trade-off: `sum()` is NOT atomic — it reads base + all cells without synchronization, so concurrent increments may produce a slightly stale sum. Use LongAdder when: high write contention, exact real-time sum not required (counters, statistics, metrics).

**In simple words (banking analogy):** **AtomicLong** = ONE shared counter at the entrance. 100 people trying to click it simultaneously → everyone fighting over the same button (CAS retry). **LongAdder** = 10 separate counters at 10 different doors. Each person clicks the nearest counter. End of day: manager walks around and ADDS UP all 10 counters. No fighting! 10x faster! But: while the manager is adding, someone might click another counter → sum slightly off (acceptable for daily totals, not for real-time balance).

**One line to remember:** LongAdder: per-thread striped cells → zero contention → 5-10x faster than AtomicLong. sum() = base + Σcells (not atomic). Use for counters/metrics. AtomicLong for exact real-time value.

sections.s3_banking: **Problem — The API gateway tracked requests/second using `AtomicLong.incrementAndGet()`.** 200 threads incrementing simultaneously → CAS retries under contention → counter overhead: 15% of CPU. Throughput limited by counter contention! Fix: `LongAdder.increment()` → each thread increments own cell → zero contention → counter overhead: <1% of CPU. `sum()` called every second for Grafana metric — slight staleness acceptable for monitoring.

sections.s5_journey:
**Step 1 (low contention).** Thread-1 calls `increment()` → CAS on `base` succeeds → base = 1. Like AtomicLong. Fast.

**Step 2 (high contention).** 100 threads call `increment()`. CAS on base FAILS for most. Thread-5: gets Cell[2] → CAS on Cell[2] succeeds. Thread-8: gets Cell[5] → CAS on Cell[5] succeeds. Each thread on its own cell → zero contention!

**Step 3.** `sum()` reads base + Cell[0] + Cell[1] + ... + Cell[N]. Not atomic: a concurrent increment might be missed. But after all threads finish: exact total.
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  ═══ AtomicLong (contention!) ═══

  Thread-1 → CAS(base, 99→100) (Recommended) 
  Thread-2 → CAS(base, 99→100) FAIL! → retry → CAS(100→101) (Recommended) 
  Thread-3 → CAS(base, 99→100) FAIL! → retry → retry → ...
  100 threads → massive CAS retry overhead!

  ═══ LongAdder (striped, no contention!) ═══

  Thread-1 → CAS(base) → Cell[0]++ (Recommended) 
  Thread-2 → CAS(base) → Cell[1]++ (Recommended) 
  Thread-3 → CAS(base) → Cell[2]++ (Recommended) 
  Each thread → own Cell → zero retry!
  sum() = base + Cell[0] + Cell[1] + Cell[2] + ...
```

```
  │  (Avoid) AtomicLong.incrementAndGet():                 │
  │     200 threads CAS on ONE variable               │
```

sections.s5d_lld:
```
  ═══ LLD — LongAdder Internals ═══

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  LongAdder extends Striped64         │
  │  - base: long (volatile)            │  low contention
  │  - cells: Cell[] (striped!)         │  high contention
  │  ──────────────────────────────────  │
  │  + increment(): void                │
  │    CAS(base) succeeds? → done!     │
  │    CAS(base) fails? → cells[hash]++│
  │  + sum(): long                      │
  │    return base + Σ cells[i].value  │
  │    NOT atomic snapshot!             │
  │  + sumThenReset(): long             │
  │    sum + reset each cell to 0      │
  └──────────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  @Contended Cell                      │
  │  volatile long value;                │
  │  // @Contended → 128 bytes padding! │
  │  // Own cache line → no false sharing│
  └──────────────────────────────────────┘

  Decision:
  Exact real-time value needed? → AtomicLong
  High-write counter/metric?   → LongAdder (5-10x faster!)
  Custom accumulator (max/min)? → LongAccumulator
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
LongAdder reduces CAS contention by striping: instead of all threads fighting over one AtomicLong, each thread increments its own Cell in a padded array. Under high contention (16+ threads): 5-10x faster than AtomicLong. Under low contention: falls back to a single base variable (same as AtomicLong). `sum()` returns base + all cells — NOT an atomic snapshot, so concurrent increments may produce a slightly stale value. Acceptable for counters and metrics, NOT for real-time balance.

Each Cell is `@Contended` — padded to its own cache line (no false sharing). `LongAccumulator` generalizes: `new LongAccumulator(Math::max, 0)` tracks the maximum across all threads using the same striping technique. In banking: API gateway request counter — AtomicLong consumed 15% CPU under 200 threads. LongAdder: <1% CPU. sum() called every second for Grafana — slight staleness acceptable for monitoring dashboards.

---

keyPoints: Striped cells reduce contention vs single AtomicLong
Under high contention: much faster than AtomicLong
sum() is eventually consistent — not exact during updates
